solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: State benefit is about right

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding

parts.note: an asset is something of benefit

explanation.surface: A sour remark that welfare payments are mostly about what you're entitled to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State benefit' reads as one welfare phrase; split it, and 'State' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to state a claim is to put it forward firmly as true.

clue.text: Request job is not started

indicators.note: something not started has had its beginning left off, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: TASK without its first letter T

explanation.surface: Someone asks for work to be done that nobody has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Request' can be a noun or a verb; the clue needs the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to put in a request for something.

clue.text: Tool I lost from small basket on bicycle

parts.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: what is lost from something is no longer in it, so the I drops out of the basket word

parts.note: a pannier is a bag or basket slung on a bike

explanation.surface: A cyclist has lost a tool out of the little basket on the bike.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a cyclist's toolkit, which is exactly where the answer would be found.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the British spanner is the tool Americans call a wrench.

clue.text: Restoration of controls on gallery male staff beginning to thieve

parts.note: the reins are the controls, as in 'take the reins'
the Tate is the London art gallery
staff who are male are men

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Security at an art gallery is being tightened after men on the staff started stealing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is London's national gallery of British and modern art, and a crossword's default 'gallery'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: restoring someone to a post or a rule to force is reinstating it.

clue.text: To walk around a bit in shoes

indicators.note: to turn around is to face the other way, so the walk word is written backwards

explanation.surface: An invitation to stroll about for a while in your shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit in shoes' reads as 'for a while'; it is the definition, a part of a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the reinforced front of a boot or shoe is one bit of it.

clue.text: Sight loon trio? That might have me excited

definitions.text: Sight loon trio? That might have me excited

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so the letters are too

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher says spotting three loons would get them worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the 'me' who would be thrilled to see three loons is a bird expert. A loon is a diver, a water bird, not a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes a bird scientist's delight at a rare sighting, which is who the answer is.

clue.text: Canine clubs Igor's running

indicators.note: things running are on the move, so Igor's letters shift about

explanation.surface: Igor is running a dog club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' reads as an adjective describing clubs; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the short-legged Welsh herding breed is one kind of canine.

clue.text: Gradual cessation of war reportedly upset male

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by word of mouth, so the word is the one that sounds like it

parts.note: peace is the end of fighting

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and out of order, so the letters of male are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gradual end to a war upsets a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' turns PEACE into PIECE, which sounds the same, and 'upset' rearranges MALE as MEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done piecemeal is done bit by bit over time, which is a gradual way of proceeding.

clue.text: Initially Kitchener has a kit inspection so some uniforms appear

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: khaki is the colour in which some uniforms appear

indicators.note: initially points to the start of each word, so the first letters are taken

parts.note: the first letters of these five words, K, H, A, K and I, spell the answer

explanation.surface: Lord Kitchener inspects the troops' kit, so they turn out in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchener was the British field marshal of the First World War recruiting poster, which suits the khaki-clad army picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is the dull yellowish-brown colour of many military uniforms, so it is how those uniforms look.

clue.text: Disconcert gunners over abandoning all cover

indicators.note: every word loses its covering, the letters at each of its ends

parts.note: the two words whose insides are kept

explanation.surface: Gunners leave their shelter, which is bound to rattle them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All' matters: both GUNNERS and OVER lose their outside letters, leaving UNNER and VE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unnerve someone is to shake their confidence, which is to disconcert or fluster them.

clue.text: Unpleasant to see guy left distraught

indicators.note: someone distraught is in a state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: It is a grim sight when a man is left in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as abandoned; it only supplies the L for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: displeasing to the eye.

clue.text: Manage to get uniform in Royal Navy

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sailor contrives to be issued a uniform in the Royal Navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manage to get' reads as 'contrive'; only 'Manage' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be in charge of a business or project.

clue.text: Journey using cycle before start of fall?

indicators.note: what comes before is placed first, so the cycle word leads

parts.note: a round is a cycle, as in a round of talks
a stumble is how a fall begins

explanation.surface: A bike ride taken just as autumn begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of fall' looks like an instruction to take F; the question mark flags a cryptic hint instead: a fall starts with a stumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an outward and return journey together.

clue.text: Gem of a game

definitions.meaning: a single diamond set on its own
a game played by one person, with cards or pegs

explanation.surface: Praise for an excellent game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gem of a game' is a compliment; split it, and both nouns are definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of being alone: a stone set by itself, and a game for one player.

clue.text: Commotion raised by one who rows on river

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it

parts.note: an oar is a rower, as in 'a good oar'

explanation.surface: A fuss started by a rower on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who rows' is a person, but crosswords use the oar itself for the rower.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a noisy public disturbance or outcry.

clue.text: A learner taking on additional confidence

indicators.note: to take something on is to take it aboard

parts.note: L = learner, from the L-plate on a learner's car

explanation.surface: A learner driver gains extra self-belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking on additional' reads as gaining more; the verb is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the spirit and self-belief of a person or group.

clue.text: Fuss over point editor took up

explanation.surface: An editor made a fuss about a point and took it up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts ADO above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: past tense of taking on an idea or cause as your own.

clue.text: Hold back, needing time for one old engineer

indicators.note: needing introduces the letter to bring in as a swap
one letter for another means a substitution, so the new letter replaces the old

parts.note: to wait is to hold back
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone told to hold back, needing time for an old engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing time for one' swaps the I in WAIT for T. James Watt was the 18th-century Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine.
explanation.definitionFit: James Watt, whose name became the unit of power, was a pioneering Scottish engineer of the Industrial Revolution.

clue.text: Outlaw road speed changes

indicators.note: a thing that changes takes a new form, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A proposal to ban changes to road speed limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' reads as a verb, to ban; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a reckless Wild West bandit is one kind of outlaw.

clue.text: Receive following second post

explanation.surface: Someone gets the next batch of mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second post' reads as the later mail delivery; 'post' is a wooden pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a pointed pole driven into the ground.

clue.text: Hunting bird's cry heard in east London

indicators.note: the Cockney accent of east London drops the H, so the word is written as a Cockney would say it

explanation.surface: The call of a bird of prey is heard in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, from east London, are famous for dropping their Hs.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the nocturnal raptor that hunts mice and voles.

clue.text: Cause of chemical change damaged a green tree at first

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so the letters are too
at first means at the start

explanation.surface: A chemical has harmed a green tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a chemical spill, and the answer is the very substance that did it.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a substance added to bring about a chemical reaction.

clue.text: Bury losing the first of season

indicators.note: to lose the first is to be without the opening letter, so the W goes

explanation.surface: Bury, the English football club, has lost the opening match of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester with a football club; the capital is only there to disguise the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to place a dead body in a grave.

clue.text: Fish that's regularly greasy

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so take every other letter

explanation.surface: A fish that is always oily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' reads as 'always'; it picks every second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the flat, winged sea fish related to sharks and skates.

clue.text: Rather small-minded welcoming king

explanation.surface: A grudging remark that someone was petty in the way they received the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather' looks like it qualifies 'small-minded'; it is the definition, as in 'pretty good'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb synonym: 'fairly' or 'quite', as in a tiring day that leaves you rather worn out.

clue.text: Dog breaking in where pigs are heavy to eat

indicators.note: in means going inside, so the rearranged letters are placed within the word for where pigs are

parts.note: pigs are kept in a sty

indicators.note: breaking means smashed apart, so the letters of dog are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog breaks into a pigsty where the swill is heavy going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' rearranges DOG into ODG, which goes 'in' STY.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodgy food is dense and filling, like suet pudding, and sits heavily in the stomach.
